title: FM and Wavetable synths
thisBuild: The Synth tab has two new kinds beside Analog. Tap the kind at the top to switch (it starts from that kind's first preset; Undo brings back what you had).

FM: four sine operators that bend each other. Pick an Algorithm (who bends whom), then Brightness for how hard, Feedback for grit, a Ratio per operator, and each operator's own envelope. Presets: E piano, Bell, FM bass, Brass, Marimba, Organ, Metal, Growl, Glass pad.

Wavetable: one oscillator that moves through a table of shapes. Six tables (Basic, Pulse, Sweep, Vowels, Hollow, Grit). Position picks the shape; Env to position and LFO to position move it while the note plays; Warp folds it. It has Analog's filter and envelopes. Presets: Vowel pad, Sweep lead, PWM strings, Hollow keys, Grit bass, Morph pluck, Vowel talk.
Making a synth now offers every preset of every kind.
From build 63: the Synth tab with Analog (Poly, Mono, Acid), Simple, Full and Synthipad.
watch: Play the E piano and Bell presets on keys with a few fingers.
Try Vowel talk in Mono on steps, and turn Position on Vowel pad while a chord holds.
Switch a synth pad between kinds and use Undo: steps and Roll notes on the pad should stay.
limits: Granular, drum and pluck synths come next.
FM has no filter of its own (the pad's Tone and effects still work on it).
A synth is mono out of its voice; no stereo spread yet.
